flashcards.q: List Azure's compute ladder from most control to most abstraction.
flashcards.a: Virtual Machines -> VM Scale Sets (VMSS) -> App Service -> Container Apps -> AKS. Control decreases and abstraction increases left to right; the decision axis is how much orchestration complexity the team is willing to own.

flashcards.q: What's the key trap in how an App Service Plan bills multiple apps?
flashcards.a: An App Service Plan is SHARED capacity across every app deployed to it -- a traffic spike on one app competes for the same instance pool as every other app on the plan, unlike Lambda-style per-invocation isolation.

flashcards.q: Compare VMSS Flexible vs Uniform orchestration mode.
flashcards.a: Flexible mode (2026 default) mixes up to 5 different VM sizes including Spot alongside on-demand in one scale set and integrates like individual VMs with Load Balancer/App Gateway. Uniform mode (legacy) requires all instances identical.

flashcards.q: State the VMSS instance count limits and what determines which applies.
flashcards.a: Up to 1,000 instances for standard marketplace/custom images via Azure Compute Gallery; capped at 600 instances if using a plain managed image.

flashcards.q: How does Container Apps scale, and what determines the scaling triggers?
flashcards.a: KEDA-driven, supporting 60+ event-source scalers (HTTP concurrency, Service Bus/queue depth, Cosmos DB change feed, Kafka lag, cron). minReplicas:0 gives true scale-to-zero; the first request after idle pays a cold-start tax.

flashcards.q: State Container Apps Consumption plan pricing (mid-2026).
flashcards.a: ~$0.000024/vCPU-second + $0.000003/GiB-second active; ~$0.000008/vCPU-second + $0.000001/GiB-second idle; $0.40/million requests after 2M free/month; free grant of 180,000 vCPU-s + 360,000 GiB-s/month per subscription.
Max 5,000 nodes/cluster across all node pools, max 100 node pools/cluster, max 1,000 nodes per individual VMSS-backed node pool, max 5,000 managed clusters/subscription.

flashcards.q: What changed about AKS quota starting September 2025?
flashcards.a: AKS began enforcing region-level quota on the number of managed clusters AND on specific node VM SKUs a subscription can use -- separate from and in addition to the older per-cluster node/pool limits.

flashcards.q: State the three AKS control-plane pricing tiers.
flashcards.a: Free ($0/hr, no SLA, ~10-node recommended cap, dev/learning only), Standard (~$0.10/cluster/hour, 99.95% SLA), Premium (~$0.60/cluster/hour, adds Long Term Support).

flashcards.q: What is Node Auto-Provisioning (NAP) and what does AKS Automatic bundle with it?
flashcards.a: NAP is Karpenter-style just-in-time node provisioning that watches for unschedulable/pending pods and provisions right-sized nodes without pre-configured node pool shapes. AKS Automatic bundles NAP with managed system node pools and a financially-backed pod readiness SLA (99.9% of qualifying operations complete within 5 minutes).

flashcards.q: Compare Container Apps scale-to-zero to AWS Fargate.
flashcards.a: Container Apps scales to zero replicas and near-zero cost during idle; Fargate has no scale-to-zero concept -- minimum running task count is 1 whenever a service is on, billing continuously even when idle.

flashcards.q: Explain the App Service deployment slot swap mechanism and its main failure mode.
flashcards.a: A slot is a fully separate live app sharing the plan's compute; a swap flips routing after warming up the target slot via applicationInitialization probes -- in principle zero-downtime. Failure mode: if warm-up isn't configured or doesn't cover real startup work, traffic hits a not-actually-ready instance right after the swap, causing an error burst.
